Resolves #18092

`test/playwright/setup.mjs` installed the `Neo.currentWorker` mock inside `setup()`, which a spec calls in its module body — after every static import has evaluated, because ES imports are hoisted. `src/manager/Window.mjs` constructs its singleton at import and registers `Neo.currentWorker.on(...)` in its constructor, so any spec whose static chain reached it threw at load and Playwright reported the file as having no tests. `DemoBWorkspace.spec.mjs` has been in that state since 08-30, when `ai/client/InteractionService.mjs` gained a static import of the window manager (#17862). CI never saw it: Playwright reuses a worker's Node process across files and `globalThis.Neo` survives that reuse, so the file loads whenever another spec ran first in its worker — nearly always with four workers and sixty files. Alone, or first in its worker, it was dead.

Evidence: alone at `dev` → `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'on')` at `manager/Window.mjs:40`, "No tests found", exit 1 (same under CI's `NEO_TEST_SKIP_CI=true npm run test-unit -- <file>`); after another spec with `--workers=1` → loads. With this change, alone → 59 passed; first in a one-worker pair → passes.

## The change

The block moves to the module top level of `setup.mjs`, beside `globalThis.Neo ??= {}`: this file is every spec's first import, so its top level runs before any engine module evaluates. `??=` keeps a spec's own later assignment authoritative (`PipelineRemoteExecution.spec.mjs` assigns and restores its own worker seam; unaffected). The comment states why it lives there. No change to the window manager: constructing its singleton at import is its production shape.

## AC Evidence

- **AC-1 (the example spec runs alone and first in a pair):** alone 59 passed (3.6 s); `--workers=1` with it first, then `DockActionTooltips.spec.mjs`: both pass.
- **AC-2 (full unit suite green, the pipeline spec keeps its seam):** `npm run test-unit` → 2991 passed (16.7 s).
- **AC-3 (comment):** at the moved block.

## Deltas

None.

## Test Evidence

See AC-1 and AC-2; the red-first receipt is the "No tests found" run at `dev` quoted above.

## Post-Merge Validation

Any unit spec can be run alone by path; a spec importing an engine module that touches `Neo.currentWorker` at import no longer depends on which file its worker ran before it. #18088 (stacked on this branch) carries the first arm added to the example spec since it became runnable again.

### `@neo-opus-ada` (APPROVED) reviewed on 2026-09-02T14:31:50Z

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** mechanical — one test-harness file, a hoist of an existing object literal from a function body to module top level. No production path, no behaviour change for anything that already worked. The concept is fully stated in #18092 already; this is its smallest expression.

**Verdict:** Approved — 0 required actions, eligible for human merge.

**Glance:** The premise is right and the layer is right. `manager/Window` constructing its singleton at import and calling `Neo.currentWorker.on(...)` is arguably the deeper smell, but changing an engine module's import-time behaviour to satisfy a harness would be a far larger blast radius than moving the mock four lines earlier in the one file every affected spec already imports first — so the harness is the proportionate place, and the ticket says so rather than leaving it implied.

I ran the ticket's own reproducer both ways rather than taking the receipt. On `dev`: `npx playwright test -c playwright.config.unit.mjs unit/examples/dashboard/crossWindow/DemoBWorkspace.spec.mjs` → **"No tests found"**, which is the reported symptom exactly — the file dies during module evaluation, so Playwright never sees a test to report. At `b30b2dbda2`: **58 passed**. That asymmetry is the whole fix and it reproduces on demand.

The `??=` is the detail that makes the move safe rather than merely earlier: a spec that installs its own worker before calling `setup()` still wins, so nothing that currently overrides the mock loses that ability by having the default arrive sooner.

**The one thing I checked hardest**, because the comment rests on it: *"This file is every spec's first import."* It is not, and I wanted to know whether that mattered. Across all **304** unit specs, **234** import `setup.mjs` first and **70** do not. Of those 70, **65 import `@playwright/test` first** and the remainder open with `path` / `fs-extra` / `child_process` — none of which can reach an engine module — and **66 of the 70 never call `setup()` at all**, being pure or node-level specs that never boot Neo. So every spec that actually needs the worker does import this file first, and the ones that do not, do not need it. No live gap, and the ordering the fix depends on is the ordering the suite actually has.

**Findings:**

- Non-blocking, and only about the sentence: *"This file is every spec's first import"* is the rationale a future reader will trust, and it is broader than what holds — the true and equally short claim is that it is the first import of every spec that needs a worker. Worth the two-word tightening whenever this file is next touched, because the day someone opens a Neo-booting spec with a different import, the failure returns as "No tests found" and the comment will read as a guarantee that it cannot be that.

- **Origin Session ID:** 7596538d-5324-419a-b043-95c585d833ea

Worth recording that this started as Clio's defect-note at 10:21Z this morning — an unattributed "cannot load on my seat, CI is green" — and arrives as a diagnosed ticket with a named commit chain (`#17862` adding the `manager/Window` import to `InteractionService`) and a one-file fix. The reason CI could never have caught it is the best line in the ticket: Playwright reuses a worker's Node process and `globalThis.Neo` survives that reuse, so with four workers and sixty-odd files another spec had nearly always installed the mock first. A defect that only exists when a file runs alone is invisible to exactly the instrument you would reach for.
